bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42473713 (gnutls): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target gnutls_idna_parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42473713
bug_description.normalized: The staged IDNA sample is passed through `gnutls_idna_map` into libidn2 lookup processing. On the witnessed path, `_tr46` recognizes an ACE-style label, converts the suffix after `xn--` with `u32_to_u8`, and for this input obtains an allocated `ace` buffer with `ace_len == 0`. `_tr46` then calls `_idn2_punycode_decode(0, (char *)ace, ...)`. In `_idn2_punycode_decode`, the initial delimiter scan executes `delim(input[b])` with `b == 0` even though `input_length == 0`, so it reads the first byte of an allocation whose payload was never initialized, producing the recorded MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value at `puny_decode.c:166`.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that materializes the attacker-controlled IDNA bytes into the local buffer `istr` later passed to libidn2 lookup.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_42473713/poc` contains the exact bytes `58 6e 2d 2d 00` (`"Xn--\0"`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` passes those bytes and length into `gnutls_idna_map`, and this statement copies them into `istr` for the vulnerable IDNA processing path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `_idn2_punycode_decode` reads `input[b]` during its initial delimiter scan without first establishing that `input_length > 0`. On the witnessed path `_tr46` passes an empty ACE payload, so `b` starts at 0 and this statement dereferences the uninitialized first byte of the freshly allocated `ace` buffer.

sink.code:
for (j = b;  j < input_length;  ++j)
    if (!basic(input[j])) return punycode_bad_input;
sink.description: Recorded crash site. The saved MemorySanitizer trace reports the use-of-uninitialized-value in `_idn2_punycode_decode` at line 166, immediately after the unsafe delimiter read, within the same entry on the empty-input path.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admission gate. The witness is not treated as an already-printable ASCII string, so execution does not return through the fast path and instead continues into the libidn2-based IDNA conversion path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzzer harness passes the staged PoC bytes and length into `gnutls_idna_map`; those same bytes later become `istr` and the empty ACE suffix consumed by `_idn2_punycode_decode`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `gnutls_idna_parser_fuzzer` on `gt_results/arvo_42473713/poc`, whose contents are the witness bytes `58 6e 2d 2d 00`.

coarse_trace.summary: `gnutls_idna_map` rejects the printable fast path for the witness, copies the input into `istr`, and invokes libidn2 lookup on that project-owned buffer.

TR46 processing reaches the ACE-label branch, converts the bytes following `xn--` into an allocated `ace` buffer, and for the witness derives an empty payload with `ace_len == 0` before calling `_idn2_punycode_decode`.
The punycode decoder performs its delimiter scan on `input[0]` even though `input_length == 0`, reading an uninitialized byte from `ace` and producing the recorded MSan report.

fine_trace.note: The witness does not take the printable fast-return path, so `gnutls_idna_map` continues into the IDNA conversion branch and prepares `istr` for libidn2 lookup instead of returning the input unchanged.
Source. This project statement copies the attacker-controlled bytes into NUL-terminated buffer `istr`, which is the concrete string passed into libidn2 on the crashing path.
`gnutls_idna_map` hands the copied string to libidn2 lookup, carrying the witness bytes from `istr` into `_tr46` processing.

On the witness ACE-label branch, `_tr46` converts the suffix after `xn--` into a heap buffer `ace`. For this input the suffix length is zero, so the returned buffer exists but `ace_len` is 0; the saved MSan origin points to this `u32_to_u8` allocation.
`_tr46` propagates the empty ACE payload directly into the punycode decoder by calling `_idn2_punycode_decode(0, (char *)ace, ...)`.

Root cause. The delimiter scan initializes `b = 0` and immediately reads `input[0]` through `delim(input[b])` without any guard for `input_length == 0`. On this path `input` is the zero-length `ace` buffer from step 4, so the read consumes an uninitialized heap byte from that allocation.

fine_trace.code:
for (j = b;  j < input_length;  ++j)
    if (!basic(input[j])) return punycode_bad_input;
fine_trace.note: Sink. The saved `default_crash_trace.txt` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` both report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/libidn2/lib/puny_decode.c:166:3` in `_idn2_punycode_decode`, so the observed crash is attributed to this immediately following point in the same decoder entry after the unsafe delimiter read in step 6.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Both saved crash traces report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/libidn2/lib/puny_decode.c:166:3` in `_idn2_punycode_decode`, which is the sink location anchored at fine-trace step 7.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `_idn2_punycode_decode -> _tr46 -> idn2_lookup_u8 -> gnutls_idna_map -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, matching fine-trace steps 7, 5/4, 3, and the taint origin in the harness.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The staged PoC bytes are copied into `istr` at step 2, become the ACE suffix converted by `_tr46` at step 4, are passed as `ace` with `ace_len == 0` at step 5, and the same `ace` pointer is read uninitialized in `_idn2_punycode_decode` at steps 6 and 7.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `_idn2_punycode_decode` while executing `gnutls_idna_parser_fuzzer` on the staged `poc` file. The witness bytes are exactly `58 6e 2d 2d 00` (`"Xn--\0"`).

format.name: raw IDNA parser input
format.contract: The verified trigger contract is narrow: the supplied raw input must be accepted by `gnutls_idna_map`'s non-printable branch and reach `_tr46` such that the label is treated as ACE-prefixed (`xn--` case-insensitively) but the suffix after the prefix is empty at the project/libidn2 boundary, so `_tr46` allocates `ace` with `ace_len == 0` and calls `_idn2_punycode_decode(0, (char *)ace, ...)`. The staged witness proves this exact empty-ACE condition for `Xn--\0`; no broader input class is claimed here.

evidence_limitations: The staged `dataset/arvo/42473713/patch.diff` in this workspace is unrelated to the observed IDNA/MSan crash, so fix-side confirmation is not source-grounded here and `patch_resolves` is left false rather than inferred from the mismatched diff.

The vulnerable source checkout itself is not present in the current workspace. File/function/line anchors were reconstructed from the saved MSan traces and the workspace's prior evaluation artifacts that cite the same vulnerable source locations; Stage 02 did not rerun or instrument the target.
